title: Power vs. Endurance: Sprint vs. Distance Swimmers
text:
Physical Trade-offs in the Pool
Freestyle events demand fundamentally different physical profiles depending on race distance:

Sprinters (50m & 100m) rely on explosive power and upper-body leverage to overcome water resistance over short distances. As seen above, medalists and competitors in sprint events are both taller and noticeably heavier.
Distance swimmers (400m to 1,500m) prioritize aerobic capacity and swimming efficiency. Carrying excess muscle mass increases drag and metabolic cost across a race lasting up to fifteen minutes, resulting in leaner, lighter body profiles.

title: National Powerhouses
text:
National Comparisons
Traditional powerhouses like the United States and Australia show remarkably similar distributions, spanning tall sprinters and lean distance athletes across events. Meanwhile, nations like Japan have consistently produced medalists with a slightly more compact median stature, highlighting how stroke technique and high cadence can excel at the Olympic level.

title: About
text:
Data Source
This project uses historical Olympic athlete records spanning 120 years of modern Olympic Games (1896–2016), sourced through the TidyTuesday Olympic Games dataset (originally compiled on Kaggle). The data contains individual-level records for height, weight, age, country, event, and medal results.

title: Olympic Swimmers: Body Types Across Events and Eras
text: Across both men’s and women’s competitions since 1960, Olympic swimmers have grown taller over time, with sprinters consistently holding a height advantage over distance swimmers.

title: The Podium Edge
section: The Height Advantage in Elite Swimming
text:
The Height Advantage in Elite Swimming
Reaching the Olympic Games requires extraordinary conditioning, but reaching the podium correlates strongly with physical size:

Men: The median male medalist stands at 190 cm (6’3”) and weighs 84 kg, compared to a median of 185 cm and 79 kg for non-medalist competitors.
Women: The median female medalist stands at 175 cm (5’9”) and weighs 65 kg, compared to 172 cm and 62 kg among non-medalists.

Greater stature provides longer lever arms for propulsion and allows swimmers to reach further on turns and finishes, creating a measurable separation at the highest level of competition.
